messages:
Alex: Heads-up — Enterprise X asked for an enterprise commit proposal. Their traffic profile: ~1.2M generated tokens/day steady, typical seq=256, but they have batch overnight jobs that create ~4x spikes for 30–90m. Asking about reserved GPUs + autoscale policy + pricing impact. Who can run a quick capacity sketch?
Maria: I can take the first pass. Quick clarifying Qs: are the spikes synchronous (single customer/region) or spread across AZs? Also what model family are they expecting to pin?
Alex: Mostly single-region, single-tenant per POC. They want an Llama2-70B-like open model (quantized) or a similar 70B variant. Region: us-west-2.
Raj: Estimating GPU needs. Baseline: 1.2M tokens/day -> ~50k tokens/hour steady (24h). At seq=256, that's ~200 requests/hr if avg 256 tokens gen? Wait, need request rate calc: if avg completion is 256 tokens, tokens/sec produced per gpu varies. For a 70B quantized on A100-like GPU we can approximate 30-40 tok/s sustained. Using 35 tok/s -> one GPU can handle ~126k tokens/hour. So steady 50k/h fits on 1 reserved GPU.
Katie: For spikes 4x (200k tokens/hour) -> need ~2 GPUs (200k/126k ≈1.6). Recommend commit of 2 reserved GPUs to meet steady+spike with margin. Add 1 prewarm/standby slot for AZ failover or prewarm warmup.
Jonah: Pricing note: reserved GPUs pricing model: monthly commit with overage at on-demand rate. If they want 24/7 headroom for compliance, commit 2 + 1 burst credit pool. If they want cost-savings, commit 1 + autoscale to 3 with burst credits (but overage costs could spike).
Maria: Operational runbook suggestions:
- Autoscale policy: target_utilization=0.65, cooldown=120s, max_instances=4, min_instances=1
- Prewarm policy: warm on canary deploys and before scheduled batch windows (cron)
- Fallback: route to a smaller 13B model for non-blocking traffic when capacity constrained

Sample autoscale snippet to show the customer:
```
policy:
  metric: token_throughput
  target: 0.65
  cooldown_sec: 120
  min_instances: 1
  max_instances: 4
  prewarm_windows:
    - cron: "0 22 * * *" # prewarm for nightly batch
```

Raj: Quick reliability math: if they commit 2 GPUs and keep max_instances=4, we can absorb a single-GPU AZ outage (if AZ spread is possible) or handle software OOM with fallback. If they want strict SLA for spikes, recommend commit 3 so spikes don't trigger on-demand.
Alex: Customer asked about token-level billing vs GPU commit amortization. Can we show a 3-month cost model?
Jonah: I'll draft a 3-month P&L: baseline commit 2 GPUs = X/mo, commit 3 GPUs = X+Y/mo but reduces on-demand overage by ~Z% given their spike profile. Need actual price numbers from finance to fill X/Y/Z.
Katie: Security question raised during the meeting: can Private deployment be used for POC? They prefer VPC with KMS. If we run Dedicated, we can enable customer-managed KMS and audit logs — note potential lead time ~2 weeks.
Maria: Action items: @Jonah - prepare 3-month cost scenarios (2 vs 3 GPUs + on-demand overage), @Raj - run a microbench with our quantized 70B on a representative instance to confirm 35 tok/s assumption, @Katie - check prewarm automation ETA and KMS checklist, @Alex - share customer's exact batch schedule and any compliance constraints.
SRE Bot: deploy-bot: prewarm job scheduled for 2026-05-10T22:00:00Z per requested cron.
Alex: Thanks — I'll loop in the customer with the rough recommendation (commit 2 GPUs + burst credits, prefer commit 3 if they require guaranteed spike SLAs). Follow-up meeting scheduled Tuesday 10am PT.
Maria: I'll post the capacity calc and cost skeleton into the deal playbook before EOD. :memo:
Raj: Will run bench tomorrow and report peak tok/s and memory usage.
Jonah: I'll coordinate with finance for SKU rates and send slides before Tuesday.
Katie: Noted on KMS lead times. I'll ping infra-provisioning for priority slot. :thumbsup:
Alex: Great, thanks team.
